name: Question 10
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=3y,\,y(0)=1
$$

Suppose we wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={e}^{3x},$ compute the local truncation error ${τ}_{1}$ for the first step starting at $x=0$ with step size $Δx=0.2.$ Round your answer to three decimal places.

${τ}_{1}≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact $y$-value at the start of the step $x=0$ is $y(0)=1.$  Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method.

First, the slope at the start of the step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(0) & =3{y}_{\text{exact}}(0) \\  & =3\cdot 1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the increment at this step is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(0)\cdot Δx \\  & =3\cdot 0.2 \\  & =0.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(x+Δx) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(0+0.2) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(0.2) \\  & ={e}^{3\cdot 0.2} \\  & ={e}^{0.6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for the first step starting at $x=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{1} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-(y(0)+Δy) \\  & ={e}^{0.6}-(1+0.6) \\  & ={e}^{0.6}-1.6 \\  & ≈0.222\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a single step of a numerical method, when the step begins from an exact value. The LTE of a numerical method at step n from x with exact value yexact(x) to xnew=x+Δx is τn=yexact(xnew)−ynew=yexact(xnew)−(yexact(x)+Δy).

We're given that the exact y-value at the start of the step x=0 is y(0)=1. Now, let's find the y-increment given by the numerical method.

First, the slope at the start of the step is yexact′(0)=3yexact(0)=3⋅1=3.

So, the increment at this step is Δy=yexact′(0)⋅Δx=3⋅0.2=0.6.

Next, we compute the exact value at xnew:

yexact(xnew)=yexact(x+Δx)=yexact(0+0.2)=yexact(0.2)=e3⋅0.2=e0.6.

Finally, we calculate the LTE for the first step starting at x=0:

τ1=yexact(xnew)−(y(0)+Δy)=e0.6−(1+0.6)=e0.6−1.6≈0.222
